English speakers often try to map this Spanish pattern onto English word-for-word, and that is exactly where Unit N starts. Open with **why the English habit fails**, then name the Spanish form you will teach.

This is **Unit N of the A1 Spanish course** (*Title*). By the end you will be able to [can-do in one sentence].

> **Workbook (answered exercises):** [Unit N exercises](/blog/curso-espanol-a1/unidad-N-slug-ejercicios-soluciones)  
> **Previous:** [Unit N–1 title](/blog/curso-espanol-a1/previous-slug)  
> **Next:** [Unit N+1 title](/blog/curso-espanol-a1/next-slug)

---

## What you will be able to do

After this unit you can:

- Communicative can-do 1 (observable).
- Communicative can-do 2.
- Communicative can-do 3.
- Spot the typical English-speaker error with this structure.

---

## Grammar

Explain the form in English. Use a paradigm table. Give **12–20** Spanish examples, each glossed once:

[[Me llamo Alex.|My name is Alex.]]

Keep one main structure. Support forms only if the can-do needs them.

### Form

| Person | Spanish | English |
|--------|---------|---------|
| yo | | |
| tú | | |
| él / ella / usted | | |
| nosotros / nosotras | | |
| vosotros / vosotras (Spain) | | |
| ellos / ellas / ustedes | | |

### Use

When English does X, Spanish does Y. Give minimal pairs.

---

## How English and Spanish differ here

Write a contrast section. Show a **literal English calque**, mark it as wrong, and give the natural Spanish. This section is not optional: it is the pedagogical core for this audience.

- × *Soy 25.* → [[Tengo veinticinco años.|I am twenty-five years old.]]

---

## Vocabulary

Teach **12–20** items **in sentences**, not as a naked list. Reuse the unit topic (family, café, city…). Note gender of every noun: *el / la*.

| Spanish | Gender / extras | Example | English |
|---------|-----------------|---------|---------|
| | | | |

---

## Pronunciation and spelling

Cover stress, written accent, and any sound English does not have (*ñ*, *j*, *rr*, vowels). One short listen-and-repeat set (even if audio lands later).

---

## Model dialogue or reading

A short authentic-feeling text at A1 (60–120 words) or a dialogue (8–12 turns). Gloss the whole block. Then 3 comprehension questions (answered in the workbook, previewed here).

---

## English-speaker pitfalls

At least five:

1. × wrong → [[correct Spanish.|English]]
2. …
3. …
4. …
5. …

---

## A 15-minute practice plan

1. Re-read the paradigm aloud (3 min).  
2. Cover the English column and recall (5 min).  
3. Do Grammar items 1–8 in the workbook without looking (7 min).
